newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dollar, sentiment sustain Brussels bourse rise.
newsitem.headline: Dollar, sentiment sustain Brussels bourse rise.

text.p: The strong dollar, hedge trading of several new instruments and sound fundamentals combined on Tuesday to lift the Brussels bourse, and traders said they foresaw the rise continuing for several days.
"The dollar sensitives are all strong, but the whole market is rising and we could seen this movement to the end of the week," one trader said.

At 0915 GMT the Bel-20 index of blue chip shares was 14.67 points or 0.65 percent higher at 2,283.98, with 16 gainers, two unchanged and two losers. A total of one billion francs of Belgian shares had changed hands.

The dollar has been rising against European currencies following the victory of Left wing parties in the French election which raised questions over the ability of the European Union to follow through its single currency project on schedule.

Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere, which is very sensitive to dollar movements, was up 1.03 percent to 2,950 francs, steel cord and wire maker Bekaert was 0.83 percent higher at 21,300 francs, and retailer Delhaize was up 1.1 percent to 1,825 francs.
Banks too were cruising smoothly. Kredietbank and BBL were up 1.5 and 1.3 percent respectively.
Oil major PetroFina was the market leader by value, with the stock unchanged at 12,450 francs in a volume of more than 30,000 shares.

However, traders said the stock was completely stymied by the expiry this afternoon of warrants giving holders the option to buy shares at 14,500 francs. They said they expected efforts to try to boost the market price.
There was also underlying support in the market from a series of new trading instruments which were being actively hedged and would continue to be so, traders said.
